_comment: Technical Design v0.38's Setting Pack: Il Notaio's notes, then code's private and action lines, as templates. Code fills the {named} placeholders and nothing else ({currency} is the setting's plural). Copied verbatim from the engine (CC-20261111-04), so every game replays unchanged; rewording one is a content change, version-gated like a prompt. The placement lines are still stand-ins until TD drafts Il Notaio's event templates.

notes.attendance: Tonight is a smaller gathering than most: only {cast} attend. {absent} are alive, but elsewhere tonight, and can't be reached.
notes.new_group: {actor} and {other} returned to company and formed a new group.
notes.withdrawal: {actor} drew {other} aside from company — a private word, where none could hear.
notes.withdrawal_repeat: {actor} was once again seen withdrawing in private, this time with {other}.
notes._withdrawal_repeat_before_comment: TD v0.25 and earlier: the repeat note before v0.26's rewording, kept so older games replay as they ran.
notes.withdrawal_repeat_before_td26: {actor} was once again seen drawing another aside — this time {other}. Some note it is not the first private word sought this evening.

lines.pension_taken: You accepted a French pension of {amount} {currency}. Your purse: {purse} {currency}.
lines.pension_renounced: You renounced the French pension held by {holder}: {amount} {currency} returned to the Embassy.
lines.pension_refused: Your attempt to renounce a pension for {holder} failed: no such pension that you can repay.
lines.ledger_renounced: the pension held by {holder} was renounced

hints._comment: Il Notaio's hint to the player (TD v0.40, Il Notaio's hint): a line or two for what the moment asks, in a box under the stream, styled apart from his announcements. Templates only, no model calls. Drafted by Claude Code for Dylan's review (CC-20261112-03). `council` and `ballot` are for the full game. `errandDeadline` (TD v0.47): with plot_reward on, the last round before the errand's deadline, shown whether or not the errand is done.
hints.mingling: You're among the guests. Listen, and speak when the company turns to you, or pass. Hover over anything on the screen to learn what it's for.
hints.answering: {name} has spoken to you directly. An answer is expected, though silence says something too.
hints.colloquio: You and {other} have withdrawn for a private word. No one else hears you, but everyone saw you go.
hints.move: The company is shifting. Stay where you are, join another group, or draw someone aside for a private word.
hints.seat: Your private word is over. Find a group to join.
hints.midnight: Midnight. Choose your act in secret. Every act lands at once, and no killer is ever named.
hints.council: Your faction has gathered apart. Only your own people hear what is said here.
hints.ballot: The ballot. Every guest casts one vote, and may buy more for the same candidate.
hints.refused: That couldn't be done; the reason is just above your box. The / menu shows what you can do now.
hints.errandDeadline: This is the last round before the last council. To earn your errand's extra act at midnight, it must be finished before that council begins.
hints.dead: You have died. You can still read the web, what you heard and saw, and your notes, and you'll hear the city's announcements.

reading._comment: TD v0.44, Il Notaio's reading in the Web of Secrets: the prompt in TD names him and his trade in its own words; these replace them when the prompt is loaded. His name is in-world-names.json's narrator.

room._comment: TD v0.45, Block 5's {room} (Mechanics: Everyone Sees the Room): where every other living guest is right now. Each group, then each private pair, joined by `between`, ending with `end`; a group's names joined by commas and `and`. Drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261113-04); `together` and `in private` are TD's words.
room._places_comment: TD v0.49, Named places: from TD v0.49, {room} is told place by place, each other occupied place in setting.json's order as `place` (a group, or a guest on their own) or `place_private` (a Colloquio), joined by `between`, ending with `end`; the names joined as above. `in_place` follows the conversation's kind in block 5's {conversation_label} ("a Capannello in the loggia with …"). TD's words.

name._comment: Interface v0.11, Il Notaio's name glossed: `gloss` is the caption under his name at the top of the opening; `hover` shows wherever his name appears on the screen (his notes in the stream, his hint, his reading, the tour's cards), even with the hover explanations off. His glossary entry (player.json's glossary) starts with the same gloss.
name.hover: Il Notaio: Italian for “the notary”. He records the evening and belongs to no faction.

opening._comment: Interface v0.7, The Opening: the story Il Notaio writes on a full screen before the player chooses, a paragraph at a time, in this order. Fixed text, never a model call. Lore writes it and Characters canon-checks it; until then it holds only its last line, the orientation line (Interface v0.14), and the paragraphs drop in here as the list grows (#148).
paragraphs: Speak as your character would, plainly.

tour._comment: Interface v0.8, The Tour: one card per part of the screen, in Il Notaio's voice, in the tour's order. `conversation` is step 6, the message box's card (#151 adds the warning there, Interface v0.14). `briefing` is the last: the Your briefing button, which starts the evening. Drafted by Claude Code (CC-20261114-10) for Dylan's review.

steps.sheet: This is you: your purse, the payments you've taken, how often you've drawn someone aside, and what you may do at midnight. Click your name or portrait for your briefing.
steps.decks: Your briefing, the rules of the evening, what the whole city knows, and a glossary of the evening's words. Each opens over the room, and each keeps your place.
steps.errand: Your errand: what you came to do tonight. It stays pinned here, and once it's been judged, the result shows here too.
steps.room: The room: who stands with whom. You see every group, and who has slipped away in private, but never what they say. Click a portrait to look at that guest.
steps.stageBar: The evening, stage by stage. The long one is now. Click an earlier one to read it again; nothing can be said from there.
steps.conversation: The conversation you're in, and your box beneath it. Type what your character says, and Speak. Begin with @ to address one guest, or / for what you may do instead of speaking.
steps.right: Whoever has your ear, or whoever you've chosen to look at: only what everyone at the party knows of them.
steps.web: The Web of Secrets: who is tied to whom, what you heard and saw of each guest, and your own notes. Click the bar to raise it.
